whatsHappening.background: Yemen’s current crisis escalated after the Houthi movement seized Sana’a in 2014 and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to support the internationally recognized government. A 2022 truce reduced large-scale fighting, but Yemen remains divided, fragile, and deeply affected by conflict, economic collapse, disease outbreaks, and damaged public services.

parties.name: Recognized Government
parties.description: Internationally recognized authorities backed by the Saudi-led coalition.

parties.name: Southern Forces
parties.description: Groups in southern Yemen with competing political and security goals.

parties.name: Civilians
parties.description: Families face hunger, displacement, disease, and weak basic services.

timeline.description: Houthis seize Sana’a and the political crisis escalates.
Saudi-led coalition intervenes in Yemen’s war.
A UN-backed truce reduces large-scale fighting.
Humanitarian needs remain severe despite reduced front-line fighting.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians are living through one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises. Families face hunger, displacement, disease, unsafe water, damaged health services, and limited income after more than a decade of conflict and economic collapse.

image.alt: A child carried through rubble in Yemen

howToHelp.summary: Yemen’s crisis is driven by conflict, economic collapse, disease, displacement, and damaged services. Humanitarian aid and sustained diplomacy both matter.

learnMore.text: This page explains how Yemen’s political conflict became a long humanitarian emergency.

whatsHappening.background: Yemen’s war affects civilians through hunger, disease, displacement, protection risks, and shrinking access to services. Children are especially vulnerable because malnutrition, missed school, unsafe water, and damaged health care can shape their entire future.

parties.name: Children
parties.description: Many face wasting, disease, interrupted education, and protection risks.

parties.name: Displaced Families
parties.description: Millions live away from home, often in camps or unstable shelters.

parties.name: Women and Girls
parties.description: Face higher risks from poverty, displacement, and limited services.

parties.name: Sick and Injured
parties.description: Health care is weakened by shortages, damage, and underfunding.

timeline.description: People are acutely food insecure in 2026.
Children under five are acutely malnourished.

image.alt: Children reaching for aid in Yemen

civilianImpact.experiences: Families are not only affected by direct fighting. Many cannot afford enough food, lack safe water, or live far from functioning clinics. Funding cuts and access restrictions make it harder for aid groups to reach the people facing the most severe needs.

image.alt: Children reaching for aid in Yemen

howToHelp.summary: Humanitarian support helps families survive, but lasting improvement also depends on a political solution, restored services, and sustained funding.

learnMore.text: The civilian toll includes hunger, malnutrition, displacement, health risks, and years of disrupted education.

image.alt: A child sitting near rubble in Yemen

whatsHappening.background: Support is most effective when it goes to organizations already delivering food, nutrition, clean water, health care, protection, and education support in Yemen. Public attention also matters because Yemen remains severely underfunded despite the scale of need.

parties.name: UNICEF
parties.description: Supports children with nutrition, health, WASH, education, and protection.

parties.name: WFP
parties.description: Provides food assistance and logistics for the humanitarian response.

parties.name: UNHCR
parties.description: Supports displaced families, refugees, shelter, and protection.

parties.name: Local Partners
parties.description: Help deliver aid in communities with urgent needs.

timeline.description: Support trusted relief groups serving families in Yemen.
Follow verified updates on hunger, displacement, and aid access.
Keep attention on a crisis that is easy to overlook.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping Yemen means funding emergency food, nutrition treatment, safe water, health care, and protection for displaced and conflict-affected families while supporting diplomacy that reduces harm to civilians.
